questions.question: Which region of Spain is paella originally from?
questions.fact: Paella is named after the wide, shallow pan it's cooked in: "paella" simply means "pan" in Valencian.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient in hummus?
questions.fact: "Hummus" is simply the Arabic word for chickpea.

questions.question: Which nut is marzipan made from?
questions.fact: Toledo in Spain and Lübeck in Germany are both famous for their marzipan.

questions.question: Sushi rice is seasoned with which ingredient?
questions.fact: Sushi rice is seasoned with rice vinegar, sugar and salt. Sushi began as a way of preserving fish in fermented rice.

questions.question: Which spice gives traditional paella its golden colour?
questions.fact: Saffron is the dried stigmas of a crocus flower. It takes around 150 flowers to make a single gram.

questions.question: Which pastry are profiteroles made from?
questions.fact: Choux pastry puffs up hollow because the water in the dough turns to steam in the hot oven.

questions.question: Which country does feta cheese come from?
questions.fact: Feta is protected in the EU: only cheese made in Greece in the traditional way can be sold as feta.

questions.question: Which flavour is the classic tiramisu soaked in?
questions.fact: Tiramisu means "pick me up" in Italian, probably thanks to the coffee and cocoa.

questions.question: Which fruit is cider made from?
questions.fact: In Asturias, cider is poured from high above the glass to make it lively and fizzy.

questions.question: In Spain, churros are traditionally dipped in…
questions.fact: In Madrid, a thicker cousin of the churro is called a "porra".
